title: Suarez 2013-14 v Salah 2024-25: Liverpool's best ever season?
sources: data/competition-history/premier-league.json (top scorers, top assisters, FWA winners, champions)
checked: Suarez 31 league goals, Golden Boot and PFA award, Liverpool second on 84 points two behind City, the 0-2 Chelsea defeat and the 3-3 at Palace from 3-0 up, ban carried into the season (Wikipedia season page); 13 assists and FWA award (local file, which lists Suarez and Gerrard joint top on 13). Salah 29 league goals, 34 all comps, 47 goal involvements as a 38-game record, title won 5-1 v Spurs on 27 April, 84 points (Wikipedia season page); 18 assists, Golden Boot and Playmaker (Premier League, Liverpool FC, local file).

lines.text: Same club, same shirt, same points total. One got a trophy, one got heartbreak.
Luis Suarez, twenty thirteen, fourteen. He starts the season still serving a ban.
Then he comes back and destroys everybody. Thirty-one league goals, thirteen assists.
Mohamed Salah, twenty twenty-four, twenty-five. Thirty-two years old, and somehow better than ever.
Twenty-nine goals, eighteen assists. Forty-seven goal involvements, a record for a thirty-eight game season.
On numbers it's close. Suarez scored more. Salah made more.
Both won the Golden Boot. Both were voted the best player in the country.
Now the twist. Both Liverpool teams finished on exactly eighty-four points.
In twenty fourteen, eighty-four wasn't enough. City got eighty-six. Liverpool threw away a three-nil lead at Palace.
In twenty twenty-five, eighty-four won the league with four games to spare. Five-one against Spurs.
Same points. One title. Salah has the medal.
Suarez was the better show. Salah was the better season. Settled.
